newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche CEO-more consolidation due in bank sector.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche CEO-more consolidation due in bank sector.

text.p: Increased global competition in financial markets will lead to further concentration in the German banking sector, Deutsche Bank chief executive Hilmar Kopper said on Tuesday.

The introduction of the Euro will make European financial markets clearly more attractive to institutional investors from the U.S. and Japan, Kopper said in an annual banking survey in Germany's Boersen-Zeitung newspaper.
As competition increased, there would be further concentration and cost-cutting in the banking sector, and not only in Germany, Kopper said.
"We have to identify and exploit areas where savings can be made and synergies introduced," said Kopper.
"Attempts by foreign banks to win worthwhile market share in Germany have not been very successful to date. That could change more quickly than we expect," Kopper said

"The introduction of the Euro in 1999 will accelerate this process as the disappearance of the deutschemark also signals the end of one of the most important competitive strengths enjoyed by German banks," said Kopper.

"Without competition we would probably sleep better, but live worse," said Kopper, who retires as chief executive of Germany's biggest bank in May 1997. He will be succeeded by management board member Rolf Breuer.
